memo.verdict: Neutral; park; conviction medium (a working hypothesis on the cycle's length, held with a clear view on the price). The park is on the return, not the gate: the park rule is not triggered (management C, business quality B, transmission B, trackability B). Two ways back: a price below about 4,400p (the sixty-forty blend of the record's two branches) without a change in the evidence; or below about 5,100p with two consecutive confirmations that the cycle is running (ASML's and TSMC's 2027 plans held or raised in October 2026 and January 2027; Position Measurement order intake up sequentially with the margin above 25 percent at the February 2027 half-year), which would move the record's path toward consensus and the odds on a held multiple from possible to plausible. On the modal path alone the entry that gives 20 percent a year over eighteen months is about 3,700p. The thesis is right and the price has taken it: a case to admire and to watch, not to fund at 5,660p.
case: Renishaw is a demand-inflection case in a high-quality cyclical, compelling as a thesis and not as an entry. The change is external, cyclical and large: AI-driven wafer-fabrication-equipment spending, carried by the equipment makers' published plans two years out (ASML +30 percent EUV capacity for 2027; TSMC capex +57 percent; Applied Materials doubling output by 2028 on forecasts to 2030; Lam's calendar 2026 outlook in the low US$150bn range), has reached Position Measurement, the division that sells encoders into lithography, inspection and packaging tools and holds the number one position in fibre-laser encoders for wafer inspection and number two in open optical encoders, designed in over multi-year machine generations. The division grew 26 percent to £260.9m with a 490 bp margin gain to 27.4 percent, and visibility there extended to over one quarter against a norm of one month. Because the group carries a 70 to 75 percent drop-through on incremental volume (67 percent implied in FY2026 guidance; constant-currency operating profit +62.6 percent on +17 percent revenue), the divisional growth became a 300 bp group margin gain to 18.7 percent (21.2 percent in H2) and a 30 percent rise in adjusted EPS to £1.79.

The internal change is secondary but real and survives a downturn: six of twelve internal forces at B (an external CFO who has taken the ERP, hedging and incentives in hand; two guidance raises beaten; a £21m fixed-cost saving from a 7 percent headcount cut, with incentives re-weighted to cash conversion and a three-year ROIC; the drug-delivery closure for £3m annualised and the neurosurgery sale; ASTRiA, Equator-X, LIBERTAS, FORTiS; a 70.0p special and a 5 percent ordinary rise after a decade of cash hoarding). No screen red flag. But the saving is 2.6 percent of revenue against a £41m rise in adjusted operating profit and is partly eaten by about £15m of UK wage and national-insurance inflation, so the larger part of the output change came from the cycle. The change has travelled every layer of the 'Six Layer Inputs-outputs' chain: resources, choices, actions, key operating metrics (ROIC 17.5 percent), financial statements, and the sell-side's estimates (FY2027 consensus +32.3 percent in twelve months; Jefferies +24, +33, +35 percent to EBITA on 2026-09-10; Deutsche Bank +12 percent on 2026-07-27; no named cut).

What it earns, on the record's path: FY2027 EPS £2.13 (+19 percent; revenue £920m; margin 20.3 percent; net finance income £12m; tax 22 percent; 72.8m shares), then FY2028 £2.30 and FY2029 £2.24 as the cycle plateaus in calendar 2028, 7.8 percent a year over three years, below the band; consensus £2.73 by FY2029, 15.1 percent a year, is the run-through reading. The record puts a plateau at about 60 percent (probable) and a run-through at about 40 percent (possible): Renishaw's two prior up-legs each lasted about two years before revenue went flat or fell (FY2018 peak to FY2020 -11.2 percent; FY2022 peak to three flat years with the margin from 24.9 to 14.5 percent on FactSet's basis); this up-leg began in H2 FY2025; the order book gives about one quarter; a semiconductor-manufacturer executive puts true demand at 30 to 40 percent of the order surge because of triple-ordering (2026-09-22); sensor tool vendors hold elevated component inventory with a "highly probable" near-term plateau (2026-09-02). The odds are 40 and not 20 because of ASML's 2027 capacity, Applied Materials' 2028 output, TSMC's capex, gate-all-around's about 30 percent higher metrology intensity, hybrid bonding's three-to-four-fold wafers per bit, and Renishaw's own decision to double encoder assets with a £65m to £75m budget.
counter_case: The bull case at its strongest, as the record carries it: this is a structural step-change, not a cycle. AI data-centre investment has made wafer-fabrication-equipment spending a multi-year build with customer forecasts to 2030 (Applied Materials); each new node needs about 30 percent more metrology per wafer (gate-all-around and backside power over FinFET); hybrid bonding for high-bandwidth memory uses three to four times the wafers per bit of DDR5; wafer warpage is forcing a shift from point sensors to area scanners that doubles sub-system component demand; Renishaw holds the number one and number two positions in the encoders inside those tools, designed in over generations; the company is doubling encoder capacity with a £65m to £75m budget; it has cut £21m of fixed cost; it has turned additive profitable on defence demand with its own multi-year backlog (Raytheon book-to-bill 1.77x); and it has begun returning cash under a CFO whose incentives reward it. Position Measurement accelerated to +36 to +41 percent in the third quarter. On that reading consensus FY2029 EPS of £2.73 is conservative; Jefferies sees "mid-20 percent EBITA margins feasible for the first time since FY2022" and "further margin improvement in FY2027"; the ten-year median multiple of 22.4x is the right anchor for a business whose profit mix has moved to a 27 percent-margin, design-in-protected division, and the 2017 to 2021 regime paid 27x to 33x for the same business; every semiconductor-exposed UK industrial has re-rated together; the shares at 5,660p offer 6,090p to 6,750p with upgrades to come (Jefferies, Peel Hunt, UBS). At 22.4x the eighteen-month return on the record's own path is -1.9 percent and at 27.0x +17.5 percent, 11.3 percent a year.

From the momentum side of the framework itself: three of six Headline Ratings are B, A and B; the primary 'Target Setup' fits crisply at B; the 'Foundations' are B; estimates are rising at double-digit rates a month after the results; four of six brokers are at Buy; the shares are at a 52-week high with the 200-day rising twelve of twelve months; the framework's own instruction not to be too sceptical about staircases and not to force pessimism argues that a case with this many confirmations should be a B and progressed. The market may keep paying 22x to 27x for a semiconductor-cycle name while the equipment makers keep raising guidance, and the record's plateau in calendar 2028 is a judgement, not a fact.
triggers: - The one judgement the park rests on: whether WFE demand and Position Measurement volume run through calendar 2028 without a plateau (record: plateau probable, about 60 percent; run-through possible, about 40 percent).

- Confirmations that would move the path toward consensus and the held-multiple odds from possible to plausible: ASML's Q3 results on 15 October 2026 and TSMC's October 2026 and January 2027 calls holding or raising 2027 capacity plans; Position Measurement order intake rising sequentially at the 4 February 2027 half-year with the margin above 25 percent; two consecutive such readings.

- Alarm levels: a sequential deceleration in TSMC capex in October 2026 or January 2027; Position Measurement order intake down sequentially at the half-year; H1 FY2027 group margin below 19 percent; the share price below the 200-day average of 4,504p (the level at which market catch-up with the record's concern would be confirmed); a sudden inventory build of semiconductor position encoders relative to sales; enactment of the MATCH Act or a fall in Asia-Pacific constant-currency revenue while the cycle is still rising; an announced ERP write-down.

- Invalidate levels: Position Measurement margin below 25 percent (invalidates the bull margin path); an ERP delay beyond mid-2027; two consecutive confirmations of the cycle (invalidate the record's plateau path).

- Price triggers for the park to lift: below about 4,400p on the blend of branches without a change in evidence; below about 5,100p with two consecutive cycle confirmations; about 3,700p on the modal path alone.

- What would move 'Foundations' from B to C: a first-half FY2027 in which Position Measurement order intake falls sequentially or its margin drops below 25 percent; an encoder inventory build against sales; an ERP write-down.
